bullets.title: Fed hike 25bp tomorrow: ~94-95% market odds, 10Y near 5%
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm 94-95% market pricing for a 25bp hike at tomorrow's FOMC meeting — the first hike since summer 2023 under Chair Warsh. The 10-year Treasury reached 5.002%, highest since 2007, with the curve bearishly flattening; a 20-year auction tailed 2bp with end-user demand at 83.1%, lowest since Feb 2026. JPM models five scenarios ranging from SPX -2% (Crush Inflation) to +1% (Remove 2025 Eases), with bond vol seen as a bigger headwind than yield levels outright.

bullets.title: Investor survey: 41% expect risk-on FOMC reaction, but 63% think conditions need to tighten
bullets.body: 22V survey shows 41% of investors anticipate a risk-on market reaction to tomorrow's meeting, a 'surprisingly popular' outcome per their framework — but 63% believe financial conditions need further tightening, up 33 percentage points since start of 2026. Only 35% think core inflation is on a Fed-friendly glide path. GS Economics expects a 10-8 majority for one hike vs. risk of a two-hike majority.

bullets.title: Oil +4.2% to $105.52 on Saudi, Libya, Russia supply disruptions
bullets.body: WTI surged ~4.2% to $105.52, up ~27% over the past 11 sessions, driven by Saudi Arabia canceling Yanbu crude shipments to Europe after East-West pipeline shutdown, Libya suspension, and Russian refinery cuts with Houthi momentum adding risk premium. The oil rally is the primary macro headwind pressuring consumer discretionary, restaurants, airlines, and retailers on the day. Saudi Arabia and Egypt pledged to maintain Hormuz navigational freedom.

bullets.title: Equities close lower: SPX -0.4%, NDX -0.6%; energy leads, Mag7 lags
bullets.body: SPX closed -0.4% and NDX -0.6%, extending Monday's selloff with ~70% of SPX names in the red. Energy and cybersecurity led while Mag7, software (-1.3%), consumer discretionary, retailers, and airlines lagged. Small-cap restaurants fell 6.1%, large-cap restaurants -2.8%. JPM remains bullish on Tech, Semis, and Mag7 tactically, favoring MegaCaps into the Fed print.

bullets.title: AI demand intact; NVDA and AVGO CEOs push back on slowdown fears
bullets.body: NVDA's CEO pushed back against AI doomer narratives, while AVGO's CEO expressed confidence that inference and compute demand will remain 'very strong.' GS notes economic benefits from AI may depend less on new models than continued infrastructure and productivity buildout. Separately, 61% of voters now oppose AI data center construction, and the Trump administration ordered Kalshi to remove an AI compute price tracker.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO expected early November at ~$2T valuation; NVDA mulling $10B anchor stake
bullets.body: Anthropic's market cap has reached $2.163T on tokenized exchanges (+523% since Nov 2025), with an IPO expected early November on Nasdaq led by Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs. NVDA is reportedly in talks to invest up to $10B as anchor investor in a deal that could raise $100B total. OpenAI delayed its IPO to 2027 or later citing AI safety concerns.

bullets.title: Compute futures market launching by year-end via ICE, CME, Nodal — NVDA chips as settlement basis
bullets.body: One or two cash-settled compute futures products are expected to launch by year-end, with ICE/Nodal as early entrants and CME following after a CFTC comment period closes October 20. All expected contracts will settle based on NVIDIA Hopper (H100) or Blackwell (B200/B300) compute. Market is framed as a trillion-dollar opportunity driven by 25x projected token growth over five years via inference demand.

bullets.title: CLARITY Act fails Senate cloture vote; crypto equities sold off hard
bullets.body: The Senate blocked the CLARITY Act from advancing to a full floor vote, driving Bitcoin down to $75.9K and Coinbase -10.1%. Regulatory focus may shift to SEC/CFTC rulemaking. Mizuho flags HOOD (-3% rel.) and FIG (-6% rel.) as oversold proxies — HOOD derives 80-90% of revenue from non-crypto sources, while FIG is a HELOC marketplace with no direct crypto exposure.

bullets.title: Citi CC data: Sept week 2 spending +8.9%, MTD accelerating vs. August
bullets.body: Citi credit card data shows September week 2 total spending +8.9% vs. week 1's -1.4%, with the acceleration partly attributed to Labor Day calendar timing. September MTD is running +3.5% (+5.0% ex-food), a sharp improvement from August's -1.7%. Electronics led at +13.8% MTD, followed by Cosmetics +12.2% and Home Furnishings +8.6%; Apparel (-10.6%), Athletic Footwear (-11.1%), and Jewelry (-6.4%) remain weak.

bullets.title: Conference takeaways: consumer spending 6-10% at payment processors; corporate credit in 'very good shape'
bullets.body: A multi-bank conference summary reports 6-10% spending growth at payment processors with no signs of consumer stress or deleveraging, travel and entertainment RevPAR growth at 7-8%, and household credit improving across all cohorts. Corporate credit quality is described as very good with 700bps average margin expansion in portfolio companies. Small/medium businesses are gradually increasing borrowing and capex. Retailers are using tariff refunds to reinvest in pricing rather than margins, suppressing inflation.

bullets.title: August hedge fund performance: +0.9%, systematic macro/CTA led on energy, metals, equity trends
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs August wrap shows hedge funds gained +0.9% on a global strategy-weighted basis. Systematic macro/CTA strategies topped performance on trends in energy, metals, and equities, while quant strategies posted one of their best monthly returns but saw their worst single day in over two years mid-month. Fundamental equity L/S finished slightly positive, predominantly beta-driven. The 30-year Treasury reached its highest yield in nearly 20 years amid fiscal concerns.

bullets.title: Corporate debt picture: AI borrowing at $600B but only 4% of debt stock; ex-AI sector deleveraging
bullets.body: AI-related corporate borrowing has risen from near-zero to ~$600B in 2026 but represents only ~4% of total corporate debt. The corporate debt-to-gross-value-added ratio continues to fall steeply with gross value added accelerating to an 8.25% pace, and the financing gap remains negative due to surging profitability. No evidence of credit availability tightening; implicit leasing-related leverage is flagged as a risk.

bullets.title: Private markets mainstream push: $457B in semi-liquid evergreen funds; $26T AUM projected by 2029
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes only ~4,000 of 730,000 U.S. operating companies are publicly listed, with private markets AUM expected to grow from $15T (11% of global AUM) to $26T (13%) by 2029. Semi-liquid evergreen funds now total $457B across 486 funds with over half launched in the past four years, reflecting democratization of private market access beyond institutional investors.

bullets.title: JPM bullish on IB fees and trading; Wells Fargo NIM better than expected
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects Q3 investment banking fees and trading fees up mid-to-high teens, citing 'tremendous' M&A activity and broad FICC/equities strength. Wells Fargo's CFO signaled Q3 net interest margin will be down only 1bp or flat vs. prior guidance of -3 to -4bps. Fifth Third is tracking the upper end of NII guidance, and Morgan Stanley does not view 2026 as peak earnings, targeting wealth management expansion from 2.5M to 20M households.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley August retail sales preview: +0.7% m/m headline; Q3 consumption tracking 2.2%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley expects August retail sales to rise 0.7% m/m with control group +0.6%. Q3 real consumption is tracking 2.2% q/q saar, with goods at 1.1% and services at 2.7%. Strong auto and gasoline station sales are expected to boost the headline number, while online sales are expected to reverse July weakness in the control group.

bullets.title: Empire State Manufacturing fell 13pts to 7.6; payrolls slowing to 71K/mo average
bullets.body: The Empire State Manufacturing survey declined 13 points to 7.6 (vs. 14.8 consensus), with new orders remaining positive but unfilled orders and delivery times rising. Payroll growth has slowed to a 71K three-month average in August from 81K in June, while the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1% and core CPI moderated to 2.4% year-over-year.

bullets.title: AI agentic software driving communications infrastructure demand: TWLO, NET, CRWD flagged
bullets.body: Hedgeye argues AI agents operating as autonomous 'chief of staff' layers will drive a step-function increase in SMS, RCS, and voice communications activity. TWLO provides the software rails for agent-driven communications regardless of which AI platform is used; NET, CRWD, DT, and OKTA are characterized as signal-strength longs on the agentic software infrastructure theme.

bullets.title: GS TMT desk: NDX broke below 50- and 100-dma; oil at ~$109, rates >5% weighing on risk appetite
bullets.body: Goldman's TMT desk notes NDX breached both the 50- and 100-day moving averages to the downside with oil near $109 and the 10-year above 5%. AI infrastructure stocks are trading listlessly despite positive catalysts, and the magnitude of moves in cyber vs. AI infra without defensive support is flagged as frustrating investors. Consumer tone is K-shaped: top-end (WSM) positive, bottom-end showing relative weakness.

bullets.title: Brazil election vol elevated; Goldman recommends USDBRL put spread as odds shift toward Bolsonaro
bullets.body: Prediction-market odds have shifted toward Bolsonaro and against Lula, with BRL long positioning rebuilding to 2.7 vs. a five-year average of 0.4. Despite elevated election volatility consistent with prior cycles, USD call skew has collapsed to below the 25th percentile, suggesting low premium assigned to USD upside. Goldman's preferred expression: Buy 2-month USDBRL 5.0750 Put EKO 4.80, forward ref 5.2188.

bullets.title: Lodging RevPAR: headline -6.2% YoY distorted by holidays; underlying demand 'extremely strong'
bullets.body: Mizuho's week-ended 9/12 lodging update shows a -6.2% YoY headline RevPAR decline, but calendar-adjusted results accounting for Rosh Hashanah and Labor Day timing show luxury up 13-34% daily during the week and upper upscale averaging +21% daily. September MTD total US RevPAR is tracking +4.2% YoY on a same-day basis, with economy segment leading at +9.9% MTD.
